reviews.text: 感觉所有幸存者游戏都没抓住吸血鬼幸存者的爽点，那就是形态各异武器和升级效果，再搭配卡牌效果达成各种花里胡哨的战斗方式，武器融合是一个好思路，但是融合之后的武器效果显得没有什么太大变化，目前可选的武器实在是太少，并且也没有什么特别细化的区分，如果这是做了4年的成果的话，感觉还需要海量的更新才能让游戏好玩起来，另外，这种每波固定时间再升级的玩法实在过于拖沓，完全可以地图里加商店，购买时暂停，连吸血鬼幸存者后期都加入了倍速功能，这游戏需要优化的地方还有很多很多，暂时不太推荐，至于价格感觉不算太贵，但是也并不是很值罢了。
机械教爱好者推荐入。各方面做的很细节，内容丰富，不是粗制滥造的幸存者作品。

I want to like this game, as I love the survivors-like genre games. Arms of God had an intriguing setting, combat style, weaponry, etc. The demo got me hooked for the full release. I wanted to feel like an adeptus mechanicus fighting a holy crusade as a modified doom slayer. The full release is a frustrating and disappointing mess. Slamming the cross down to start the round only to have to leave the radius because you are instantly overrun defeats the purpose of the "crux". Weaponry feels lackluster. Pea shooters and melee weapons that feel like I'm slapping enemies with a wet fish. Every upgrade is so expensive. Not only expensive in their own right, but require so many different (ingredients, I guess?) that I never felt like I could unlock *anything* worthwhile in the roughly 9 hours that I played. Some of the more important materials come from an in-mission event that felt hopeless (protecting a generator?) that I never saw the point in trying to unlock anything. The upgrades don't even make your character feel any stronger. Weapon upgrades never made any sense. Using one gun to upgrade a completely different gun based on...what? Elemental damage never seemed to stack or make any sense at all. You can lightly shock enemies like you shuffled your feet across the carpet (shock damage), turn on a the heat a little too high (fire damage), or do a slightly higher critical damage (holy damage means higher crit damage? What?). Also: why is there no true AoE weapon? In a survivor's-like? The enemies have one. Which is great when you're trying to protect the generator and that enemy gets to carpet bomb your one of two sources for super important material 3. The game never felt like it scaled. I never felt like I had a build that did any kind of damage or had any real muscle behind it. You don't even have to beat the boss: just outlast the timer. What's the point of any of it?
其实游戏挺好的，但是我遇到个莫名其妙的BUG被气笑了。 玩的久了以后升级不解锁武器位。退了从上就好了。真的气笑了。我还想说难度怎么提的这么大。 在提个意见，删除技能希望添加一个技能页。总不能每次想换个流派就挨个点，太费时费力了。希望能预存一下

[h1]Things I Like:[/h1] [b]+++ Vampire Survivors, but it's DooM:[/b] I kinda stayed away from the Vampire Survivors trend in gaming until recently when I bought this game and a few others in the genre at heavy discounts. The low prices help and so does DooM Eternal being one of my favourite games, so seeing a Vampire Survivors with a DooM coat of paint is easing me in nicely. I really like that there's plenty of permanent progression and unlocks in this game too. [b]++ Replayability:[/b] Not just through the amount of characters, levels and difficulties, but through the large quantity of acquirable buffs and weapon combos too. It is mostly RNG what choices are available, but I've already had runs go very differently to each other simply based on what character and weapon I chose at the start. Some so overpowered it's fun, some so underpowered I end up restarting after a few levels because I'm not getting good rolls for my chosen starting weapon. [b]++ Cool Characters:[/b] Several different 'Doom Guys' to choose from, all with different abilities, stats and appearances from another. [b]++ Decent Combat:[/b] What if DooM Guy had 5 arms and a gun in each of them? After ton of weapons, upgrades, stat buffs, and special abilities, you really feel the impact and strength of your character it comes together really nicely with the size of the hordes you have to deal with. You'll have a blast during your first few runs. I really liked this one ability I got where you can carry around the Crux (which is an upgradeable crucifix that sits in the middle of the map that acts as a bit of a holdout point). It felt like that super meaningful ability that gelled well with my character and pushed them into a whole new level of power. [b]+ Useful Options:[/b] Damage numbers off is a must for me, I dont need to see that dumb s#!t filling my screen, so thank you. And thanks for including the ability to toggle between console controller button prompts, it's so much better than having to mod them in myself like I've done in other games! I also appreciate the different aiming modes, sometimes I like to sit back and leave it on Auto to relax more and sometimes I feel like I can do better getting my hands dirty in Manual. [b]+ Honesty when it comes to use of AI:[/b] [REVIEW EDIT: In the very first update, mere days after release, the dev did remove the AI gen icons. They've removed AI clause in the description so you can't read it now, so here's what I wrote in this point anyway:] I am admittedly someone who rejects generative AI in all forms of art and media, not just video games. I hate it and hate when ashamed dev's hide it more-so, so their honesty here is refreshing and the promise of replacing what very little AI art assets they actually used in the game is noble and I wish more dev's did it. Point if they actually keep their word. [b]+++ Current Price:[/b] Not only was it on sale, but part of a discount bundle with a game I already own, so I was able to get it at the best possible price. [h1]Things I Dislike:[/h1] [b]--- Controller Bugs:[/b] I had some issues with the menus where I'd lose functionality using a controller, forcing me to use the mouse, and worse than that, forcing me to ALT-F4 to close the game down when there was no way to close a tutorial pop-up window. Furthermore, I chose to display PlayStation inputs and some windows still display Xbox inputs. [b]--- Very Similar Character Abilities:[/b] First five characters kinda have the same ability. They're all just a Dash with the only difference being whatever their preferred damage type is. Kinda weird right? I expected something more elaborate like a groundpound for one, a turret for another. How about a deployable shield or wall or one that can supercharge their ranged weapons for a limited time? [b]-- Uninspired Music:[/b] Ultimately quite disappointing for anyone who actually listens to metal regularly like I do. A few of the tracks can be serviceable, but most are what sounds like the cookie-cutter kinda metal you'd find on a 'royalty free' music site. The soundtrack simply isn't entertaining, unique or personal enough to even be compared to other games with metal OSTs like DooM Eternal, Killing Floor 2 or Metal: Hellsinger and so, after about 2 hours, I'm muting and putting on my own playlist. [b]-- Character Customisation Locked Behind Supporter Pack (Paywall):[/b] I'd be fine with having a few skins and stuff in the pack, but the whole feature? What a shame. [b]-- Boring Boss Fights (so far):[/b] To clarify, I've fought the several bosses so far, some twice over and they really aren't interesting. Perhaps it's the difficulty I'm on, the genre the game is in holding it back, or the large amount of buffs you have after 15 levels of building up that turn you into a meatgrinder, but I dont find myself doing anything special for bosses. Just boils down to using your ability to dodge their attacks. Apparently, some of them you don't even have to kill to pass, I've had two that just seemed to die when the timer ran out and the game gave me the win. [b]- Flaw in The Story/This Christian God:[/b] You play a dude, sent out by your religion to prevent the apocalypse by becoming a one-man killing machine; Killing demons to harvest their souls to give to God for blessings (upgrades). I'm not religious, I'm not a religious hater either. But like, with this game clearly being based on the Christian faith's God, isn't God's blessings being completely transactional in a time of great need and great evil a sin that goes directly against the religion we're portraying? Like how arms dealers benefit during wartime when people are suffering type of thing? Just thinking because, it says we're God's weapon, preventing the apocalypse, and we trade demon souls for blessings...but if you're a regular guy in this universe and cant possibly fight and kill a demon, does God kinda abandon you in your time of need or what lol [REVIEW EDIT: This got some attention and the dev replied basically saying, quote; "It's a fictional world I created. I wouldn't read too much into it or look for deep philosophical messages." and then hit me with the disclaimer you see at the start of many games 'characters/names depicted are all fiction yadayada' hahaha Apologies if I incorrectly thought your game about God, demons, hell, cathedrals, crucifixes, holy energy, divine energy etc. etc. had something to do with Christianity! :D ] [b]- Use of AI:[/b] [REVIEW EDIT: In the very first update, mere days after release, the dev did remove the AI gen icons. They've removed AI clause in the description so you can't read it now, so here's what I wrote in this point anyway:] In the AI disclosure, they say they only used it for some icons, they do look too generic too. They said they will be replacing them in the future, so points to you if you actually do that. However, a human localiser lost their job because you didn't want to pay for them and I've seen complaints from our non-English versions of the game of some errors.

Arms of God is a roguelike action game developed and published by Dark Jay Studio that places players in the middle of a relentless war between heavenly forces and the armies of Hell. Built around the popular survivor-style formula, the game distinguishes itself through its strong religious themes, emphasizing divine blessings, angelic powers, and sacred relics rather than the traditional fantasy weapons and magical systems commonly found in the genre. The result is an experience that feels familiar in structure while offering a distinct thematic identity. The core gameplay revolves around surviving increasingly dangerous waves of demonic enemies while steadily growing stronger through a vast collection of upgrades. Players begin each run with limited capabilities, but the battlefield quickly becomes a source of new powers and opportunities. Every level gained presents choices that can dramatically influence the direction of a build, allowing players to shape their character around offensive strength, defensive resilience, area control, or specialized combinations of abilities. This constant stream of progression creates an addictive gameplay loop that keeps each run engaging from start to finish. One of the game's greatest strengths is the variety of divine powers available. Rather than simply increasing damage numbers, many blessings fundamentally alter how combat unfolds. Certain abilities unleash devastating holy attacks across large sections of the battlefield, while others create protective effects that help withstand overwhelming enemy pressure. As additional upgrades are acquired, powerful synergies begin to emerge, transforming simple abilities into spectacular displays of destruction. Discovering these combinations is consistently rewarding and provides a strong incentive to experiment with different strategies. Combat remains fast and energetic throughout the experience. Enemy forces attack in large numbers, gradually filling the screen with threats that require constant movement and awareness. Success depends on maintaining proper positioning while maximizing the effectiveness of acquired abilities. As runs progress, the battlefield becomes increasingly chaotic, with holy attacks, enemy projectiles, explosions, and visual effects combining into intense encounters that demand quick decision-making. Despite the growing complexity, the controls remain accessible, allowing players to focus on strategy rather than mechanical execution. The game's visual style effectively reinforces its central theme. Heavenly powers are represented through bright celestial effects that contrast sharply against the darker demonic enemies and apocalyptic environments. This visual contrast helps establish a strong atmosphere and makes combat feel impactful. The artistic direction may not be the most technically advanced in the genre, but it succeeds in creating a memorable identity that supports the game's focus on divine warfare and supernatural conflict. Replayability is another area where Arms of God performs well. The large selection of available blessings, upgrades, and build possibilities ensures that no two runs feel exactly alike. Players can experiment with aggressive offensive setups, defensive strategies centered on survival, or hybrid approaches that balance multiple strengths. This flexibility encourages repeated playthroughs, as there is always another combination to test or a more efficient build to discover. The roguelike structure benefits greatly from this variety, helping maintain long-term interest. Boss battles provide some of the most exciting moments in the game. These encounters introduce more demanding challenges that require players to fully understand the strengths and weaknesses of their chosen build. Unlike standard enemy waves, bosses often force adaptation and careful positioning, creating memorable tests of both preparation and skill. Defeating them delivers a satisfying sense of accomplishment and serves as a clear measure of progression throughout a run. The progression system extends beyond individual sessions, offering unlockable content and permanent improvements that contribute to long-term advancement. Even unsuccessful attempts usually feel worthwhile because they help unlock additional options for future runs. This approach keeps frustration to a minimum and ensures that players are consistently working toward meaningful goals, regardless of whether they achieve complete success in a particular session. Like many games in the genre, Arms of God occasionally struggles with repetition during extended play periods. Once players become familiar with enemy patterns and available upgrades, some encounters may begin to feel predictable. Certain abilities also appear more effective than others, which can reduce experimentation for players focused purely on efficiency. However, the game's strong progression mechanics and thematic presentation do a good job of offsetting these issues. What ultimately elevates Arms of God above many similar titles is its commitment to its theme. The concept of wielding divine power against endless demonic hordes is integrated into every aspect of the experience, from visual design and progression systems to combat mechanics and character development. This cohesive vision helps the game stand out in a genre crowded with comparable gameplay structures. Arms of God delivers a satisfying blend of action, progression, and build experimentation wrapped in a distinctive celestial-versus-infernal setting. Its engaging combat, rewarding upgrade system, and impressive variety of blessings create a compelling roguelike experience that encourages repeated play. While it does not completely escape some of the repetitive tendencies associated with the genre, its strong identity and enjoyable gameplay loop make it a worthwhile choice for fans of survivor-style action games. Rating: 8/10

The game has potential and some interesting ideas, but it ultimately didn’t match my personal taste. I also learned that the game includes some assets created with generative AI. While this may not be an issue for everyone, it’s something I prefer to avoid in the games I purchase, as it doesn’t align with my personal values regarding artistic work. On Linux, the game runs, but the installation process required some additional steps due to the Unreal Engine prerequisites, which may be worth noting for other Linux users. ----EDIT---- I’d like to add a bit more context about why the use of generative AI in games matters to me personally. Based on what I currently understand, a very large portion of the data used to train many large language and image models comes from sources that were included without explicit permission from the original creators, or that rely on legal gray areas such as “fair use” (and I’m not convinced that this concept even applies cleanly in this context). For me, this isn’t about the size of a studio or about whether developers are “allowed” to use such tools. What matters to me is transparency. If a game uses AI‑generated assets, I expect that to be communicated openly. In this case, I only learned about it afterward, which left me feeling somewhat misled. I’m critical of generative AI because these models are built on the work of real artists whose creations often end up in training datasets without their consent or fair compensation. To me, this creates an indirect transfer of value from human creators to AI systems, without those artists benefiting from it. That conflicts with my personal values regarding fair artistic work, and it’s why I prefer to avoid AI‑generated content in the games I purchase.

The game loop is literally a loop. Run in a circle on each map until the timer goes off or stand in the center by your cross depending on where you're at in the 15 levels per crusade. The game looks great overall and the maps looks like they'd be far more interesting to explore then the actual gameplay. Comboing weapons seems like it would be cool but it doesn't feel like it adds much to the combat as in uniqueness. The quests/objectives for each map are pretty unfulfilling and the same 5 or 6 will be on repeat for the remaining maps. After awhile you don't even look at them and you just run in a circle until you discover whatever the objective is.

体验爽快的类土豆兄弟割草游戏 原版土豆该有的他都有，在此基础上增加了地图互动支线，既能获取局外解锁资源，也能获取局内资源，算是不错的加法。各种武器和buff数值给的挺正常，虽然没有机制解锁，构筑联动一说，但数值起来力大砖飞也蛮有趣的。 美中不足是游戏局外成长有点奇怪，各种被动buff解锁和升级居然也要靠每局游戏中的地图互动解锁，玩一个小时只能解锁两三个，有种在玩某种开放世界网游被卡进度的感觉，令人不爽啊；其次游戏打击音效待加强，武器攻击总感觉有点软绵绵的。

非常好玩的游戏，很上头，绝对值得购买，难以想象这是一个人制作的游戏，不容易，必须支持！

Finally a gritty rougelike that takes itelf and it's premise serious again. Don't get me wrong, I love a good laugh, but when every game wants to be goofy and weird, non is. Arms Of God sets it's stage and pulls through without ever trying to be ironic or taking itself not to serious [so far, I'm only 1 hour in, but I don't expect it to change]. The gameplay is fun, tho I highly recommend to turn off auto aim. That way you do actually have to aim and attack with your main weapon, making the gameplay more engaging. Only thing I dislike so far is that you're only in any arena for 90 seconds and then the upgrade screen pulls you out of the loop. It runs great on deck. However, I do prefer battery runtime over graphics. Setting everything to low, putting the resolution scale to 0.75 and locking the frames at 30 gives you over 6 hours with around 8.3W. And the game still looks and feels great. I am really looking forward to see more from this, maybe even some more sophisticated gameplay and more expansive levels.

SO much meta game content, weapons and playable crusaders makes it fun and exciting. 10/10.

The build crafting is the element that shines. The last arena top down i enjoyed was Geometry Wars and this game is just fun. Small inde games are going to be the force that saves the gaming industry. and remember kids, We war not against flesh and bone, but principalities and powers. Amen.

If you've ever wanted some Doom in your Brotato before a Vampire Survivors run this is the game for you, muchachos. Dozens of hours of content with no in-app purchases. I haven't encountered any bugs as of yet. Well worth the price tag. It passes the "one more run" before bed vibe check.

我很少给游戏写评测，准确点说这是第一次。首先我玩了50多个小时，最直观的感受就是，好玩且上头。游戏的内容以及画风非常吸引我。各种角色，武器，祝福，祈祷，能搭配出各种各样的效果。但是玩到现在感觉最大的短板还是体量太小，内容太少，虽然我知道这款游戏是一个人在做，但是成年人只看结果。而且还有相当多的地方要优化要改善。但是，我个人觉得，能做到认真听取玩家建议，并且快速地有效地进行改善的就是一款值得玩的好游戏。我会推荐给身边的朋友玩，也希望这款游戏能越做越好

目前这游戏巨坑，体验极其差劲。 局外成长解锁的武器，如果在战斗中不自己合成出来，几乎刷不出来不说，还根本不显示是哪两种武器融合才能得到，而由于祈祷有负面效果，又不能轻易试错，一旦弄错了，武器几乎就是废了，导致战斗过程极其憋屈，纯纯的花钱买罪受 另外就是游戏结算后所获得的资源，同一种资源要的巨多，而有些资源几乎就不用，又没有资源互相转化，辛辛苦苦憋憋屈屈的打完一局，出来一看，几乎啥都解锁不了。咱也不知道搞这么多资源种类有啥意义，你既然是一个人做游戏，那你不应该把这些繁琐的东西去掉么？既能提升游戏体验，又能减少自己的工作量，不是么？ 还有就是战斗中的成长，有一局我竟然从头到尾刷出的武器全是那个神圣伤害的冲锋枪，这搞什么？背包检测么？还有我用神圣伤害加成的那个角色，结果就是刷出的火焰雷电词条的东西，等我用火焰伤害的角色，就是刷出全是神圣伤害的词条，是我太倒霉？ 目前这游戏我个人是完全不推荐，等作者再更新一些东西，或者他做不动了，开了创意工坊后，大家再考虑下入手吧，否则千万不要花钱来买罪受

I sat down to "just try Arms of God for a bit" and suddenly it was 12 hours later. My phone was dead, my stomach was filing for divorce, and I was out here wielding five holy like a caffeinated Paladin of death while headbanging to the metal soundtrack. The gore is crunchy, the upgrades are addictive, and the power fantasy is absolutely cracked. **Highly Recommended.**

This review will definitely change as the game keeps being developed, but as of the moment I type it, this review is where it stands. TL:DR Gameplay is awesome, but the menus are super buggy So I'm going to give this game a recommendation. The gameplay alone warrants a thumbs up and it's a pretty solid roguelite! I'm only on nightmare now, but will definitely keep playing and progressing. Thematically, this game is absolutely epic and has a lot of character; not to mention the music is pretty dope! If you like 40k, Doom and the ''crusader'' vibes, then you should check this game out! The gameplay itself is fantastic! The weapons have a nice variety, there's the usual weapon elements and most importantly the weapons have that ''oomf'' that makes them super satisfying when cleaving hordes of demons. As far as the gameplay goes, it functions well and I'm having a blast smiting the filthy demons! Where it falls off and becomes a bit frustrating is with the menus. I have a pretty bad arm, so I play with a controller most of the time, but I really don't mind swapping to a mouse when I have to go through a menu and whatnot. Sometimes you navigate to the menu, but you're not able to actually interact with said menu unless you restart the game. Some popups just don't go away too. Now, this being said, the game is still early access, and there's no way this goes unnoticed/unchanged. I wouldn't be too concerned in the long run, but as of right now it can be frustrating. I played this game on my steamdeck as well with lossless scaling and it's a great time. It functions great and looks good! The menu issue is still there however. Overall, I recommend this game, it has character, and is a blast overall!

As a massive fan of bullet hell roguelikes who is constantly chasing the high of Vampire Survivors and Brotato, Arms of God absolutely delivers even in Early Access. I ain't looking for a story, lore, voice acting, or high-end graphics. I just want to boot up a game, theorycraft a build, and watch the screen melt. This game scratches that exact itch perfectly. What makes it great: -Build Variety: For an Early Access title, there is more than enough variety to keep you experimenting for hours -Aesthetics & Sound: The well-designed levels and art style instantly reminds you of Doom and Diablo, backed by a heavy, testosterone-fueled soundtracks -The Upgrade System: I particularly loved the weapon upgrade loop during crusades. Being able to merge identical weapons and unlock unique traits is a brilliant and fresh departure from standard genre tropes -Balanced Progression: Passive upgrades feel impactful without being game-breaking (though I still have the pricier ones to grind for) Another fantastic Early Access gem from a solo developer that hopefully keeps this momentum going until full release. I’m all in!

As a True Christian, I found Arms of God to be an unexpected gem. Its gameplay is reminiscent of fantasies I often have of slaying unbelievers with my God-given holy arsenal. I’m aware that the game is not meant to be a religious or political commentary, but I can’t help but feel more connected to my god and my nation after my playthrough. This is what it’s all about—God, guns, and freedom—and Arms of God delivers flawlessly on all three.

不出所料，狐狸尾巴又露了，玩什么砍什么。从demo到现在，没见加强和调整弱势，倒是什么强就砍什么。先用爽游骗你付款，再用更新恶心你，又一个走这种标准流程的游戏。demo在上架前夕也是大改，亦是大砍加重度肝，没有一丝对玩家时间的尊重。上架之后假模假式的说，立志给出好的游戏体验，要对无脑强进行调整，说实在的，这种假话听多了让人心里一点波澜都没有，骗骗涉世不深的玩家还行。说要给好的游戏体验，但直接把强力的砍废，连基本流程都走不完，制作人真的玩游戏吗？如果连多门类的平衡都做不好，只知道限制玩家性能，只能说明本质是一群废物。根本不建议购买。 ----------<以下2026.7.4.>---------- 西方的游戏设计者在当今迷恋和玩家作对，请放下过去“西方游戏起码品质不会太差”的滤镜。包括许多中国游戏制作人也仍然保持学习西方的惯性。我这里可以很明确的告诉各位，无论是谁，你只需要看他们是不是在搭建其他途径之后再调整超模玩法，如果直接把超模玩法砍废，连基本流程都没法走完的，一律差评。如果这个游戏是个单机游戏，只要搞削弱，直接差评。这不是教唆大家去刷差评，而是用这种方式把那些习惯拿游戏当做霸凌工具的制作人和公司请出这个行业。

The game is going through growing pains, After the hours played, I will say I have not been a fan of certain nerfs that have started to strong arm you into certain builds, I enjoyed the aspect of finding and making builds. I also do not enjoy how reliant on RNG the game is becoming to make or break a run. Primaris is a weird templar that I was happy got a nerf though, The dev had to realize how broken of a character he would be. On the other hand this game has many templars but most are just garbage compared to just 3 of them. The game needs not just nerfs on characters and stats but on enemies as well that the dev has not addressed yet. I also find that the very limited time on a map run is just annoying and it is just a race to gather as much souls as you can to gear yourself for the next 40 second stage. if you do not have a good enough ttk speed the run is cooked on the max difficulty surviving and not killing enough is still a run ending situation in a sense. Plus some inferno difficulty bosses get ridiculous like they just negate damage 2nd mini boss on act 4 inferno seems to only take so much damage at a time for instance where it feels like he is over-tuned compared to anything else in the run including the final boss. I hope I see builds being more open again in the future and I hope that they work on the formula, stages like 2 mins max not a lot of fun when time is the biggest enemy to you in this game.

一款游戏模式类似土豆兄弟的幸存者游戏，但是质量极为一般。考虑到EA版原价48也不能算便宜，故给出差评。 打通最高难度大约也就不到15小时，之后也就不想玩了，重玩价值非常一般，耐玩性一般，总体而言乏善可陈。 优点是，游戏的整体节奏把控的不错，不用刻意刷局外成长，这一点确实很不错，因为很多肉鸽游戏在这件事上做的不好。小怪设计的不错，类型足够，攻击方式多样。 缺点是，局外内容解锁太慢，我都通关最高难度了解锁不到30%。BOSS设计无聊透顶，BOSS对角色的移速有硬指标要求，不达标就是等死。最终关BOSS更是大粪，因为它的机制竟然是高频率是玩家移动操作反向，且它的伤害能秒人。角色设计也比较无趣，首先美术上这几个角色几乎没有区别，其次角色特性有趣的只有3个。 武器的升级方式是本作的一个特色，不像土豆兄弟那样只是简单低级合成高级，而是玩家自由选择组件来升级武器的某方面的属性，这种设计可以有更高的上限，可惜本作目前没能做到。所有远程弹道类武器，都是最优先射弹树和弹射次数，贯通不用刻意叠但最好有至少1点。爆炸类和近战类的我没怎么玩，但是它们理论上也是这样优先几个属性。然后就没了。最终这个系统没能体现出它的优势，非常遗憾。 在高难度下，初始减移速的角色基本玩不了，你会被前几关的小怪直接挠死，那真的是走路都在掉血。或许刷出全部局外成长能玩，但这游戏没那么高的可玩性让我一直刷。最好用的是修女，因为她初始加移速且容易刷出加移速的物品。最好用的武器是机枪以及它的升级版本，5把顶配机枪可以直接蒸发最终BOSS。注意玩机枪不要轻易降低暴击率。

The Dev made some perplexing design choices... features "feel-bad" mechanics for no discernable reason. The way you combine firearms is counter-intuitive as heck. Whoever though that it's a good idea for respecking your upgrades in a rogue-like— to refund you less than 100% of the resources?!! IDK man. Game has something of a crysis of identity. It wants to be a game /w story & regular-old-progression but also wants to be a rogue-like. On the basic difficulty, it is too easy. I never died once playing this game & did not play long enough to unlock the higher difficulties. A propper rogue-like should really make you claw at progress, to make it clear to you that metaprogression is non-negotiable to make any headway. This game seemingly makes it an afterthought. The looks & style are the highlights of the game. Expect everything else about it to be worse. It is an early-acess game, it is allowed to be extremely rough around the edges, (which it is). I sure do hope the devs will fix it & add QOL over time.
